Heyo! There are TWO active definitions of virgin wool! I’m going off WeatherWool’s blog but there is also another:

“Virgin wool is the wool taken from a lamb's first shearing. This first lot of wool from a lamb is the finest and softest wool taken from a sheep during its life. Or it is wool that has not been processed or woven. Basically any wool that has not been recycled”

I own several Filson wool garmets: jackets, pants, hats, etc. and have enjoyed them very much. I also have two Weatherwool anoraks mid weight and heavy weight. The weatherwool fabric is superior in my opinion. It's much nicer to the touch and is more wind resistant. If anyone is on the fence go with WW hands down. Filson's quality is not what it once was and their pricing is almost as much as WW. Lastly, dealing with Ralph at WW is a joy. Their customer service is impeccable. Ralph has actually answered the phone everytime I've called!  Nice video. Thanks for sharing

Weather wool is worth it! If you are an outdoorsy type, you will pay over $700 for a decent mid-range hunting rifle, and almost $1000 for a quality scope; I don't understand why WW would be considered "over-priced" for what you get. I think it just depends on how much use you get out of it and your budget. I own the Al Anorak in heavy weight lynx and mid-weight drab. I live in the arctic, spend a lot of time outdoors, and use them most of the year except for about a 2 1/2 month period in the "summer". I know friends in Norway who paid the ridiculous customs and taxes worth nearly $350 on top of international shipping and the product itself, and where absolutely chuffed with it and want more (and not rich people). On top of it all, you get the best customer service I've ever experienced. I hope this company never changes!

Michael, Weatherwool and FIlson  both made a great Made in US Wool Coat-- But there are some other brands that I think you should consider in your quest for the greatest woolen coats. Those would be Bemidji Woolen Mills out of Bemidji, MN and Johnson Woolen Mills out of John, VT. While I've never had my hands on the Bemidji, the Johnson jackets are wondergully high quality-- albiet lined with tricot-- and both have been making the jackets in-house for a hundred years or more. Might be good jackets to test out- not sure if they're made with virgin wool or not.

I love Weatherwool and i love Filson! One thing i will say about the wool is that Filson wool is so thick it never pills. You can find Filson jackets that are 50 years old with zero pilling.
